title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Aussie Broadband Person
tiers.description: Each director, officer, employee (full-time, part-time or casual) and secondee of Aussie Broadband or the Group, and each contractor and consultant whose terms of engagement apply this policy to them. Subject to the general prohibitions (insider trading, Blackout Periods, short-term/speculative trading, short selling, financing-equity conditions) without needing prior approval to deal, unless also a Director, ELG or SLG member.

tiers.name: Director
tiers.description: Each director of Aussie Broadband, including executive or managing directors. Must obtain prior written approval from the Chair and Company Secretary (or Group CEO if the Chair or Company Secretary is the applicant) before dealing, and must notify the Company Secretary of trades within 2 days.

tiers.name: Executive Leadership Group
tiers.description: Direct reports of the Group CEO. Must obtain prior written approval before dealing (same procedure as Directors) and should ensure family members and closely connected entities avoid trading in Blackout Periods, though this is only encouraged, not required.

tiers.name: Senior Leadership Group
tiers.description: Direct reports of the Executive Leadership Group. Same prior written approval requirement as Directors and ELG, with the same non-binding encouragement regarding family members.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board reserves the right to close any Trading Window at short notice, and may also permit a Trading Window at other times where it considers the market fully informed. Confidentiality of an ad hoc closure is not addressed (contrast the separate blacklist-restriction notice for another company's securities, which is given to the affected person in writing).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on using or allowing the use of any Derivative (defined to include s761D derivatives such as options, forwards, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars, and any transaction limiting economic risk) in relation to unvested securities.
rules.evidence: Aussie Broadband People must not use, or allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any unvested Aussie Broadband Securities or vested Aussie Broadband Securities that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Same absolute ban extends to vested securities still subject to disposal restrictions (e.g. escrow or minimum shareholding lock-up).
rules.evidence: Aussie Broadband People must not use, or allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any unvested Aussie Broadband Securities or vested Aussie Broadband Securities that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Once vested and no longer subject to disposal restrictions, Derivatives may be used, subject to the Policy's other rules (short-term trading, Blackout Periods, insider trading). No prior approval is required unless the individual is a Director, ELG or SLG member.
rules.evidence: once Aussie Broadband Securities have vested and are not otherwise subject to disposal restrictions, Derivatives may be used in relation to those Securities.

rules.detail: Directors must additionally obtain prior written approval from the Chair and Company Secretary before entering a Derivative over vested, unrestricted securities.
rules.evidence: individuals who wish to trade in Aussie Broadband Securities and are members of any of the following groups must first seek approval in writing from the Chair and Company Secretary of Aussie Broadband ... each Director

rules.detail: ELG members must obtain the same prior written approval as Directors before entering a Derivative over vested, unrestricted securities.
rules.evidence: the direct reports of the Group CEO (in this Policy, the 'Executive Leadership Group')

rules.detail: SLG members must obtain the same prior written approval as Directors before entering a Derivative over vested, unrestricted securities.
rules.evidence: the direct reports of the Executive Leadership Group (the 'Senior Leadership Group')

rules.detail: Hedging is not a separately named concept; it falls within limb (b) of 'Derivative' - any transaction in financial products operating to limit the economic risk of holding the securities - and is banned while unvested or restricted.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unrestricted securities is allowed as a Derivative under 9.2; Directors/ELG/SLG need prior written approval, other Aussie Broadband Persons do not.
rules.evidence: Notwithstanding the above, the use of Derivatives over vested Aussie Broadband Securities, like any other trading in Aussie Broadband Securities, must comply with the law and with the other provisions of this Policy

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement is a 'financing arrangement' using securities as effective collateral and/or an agreement to deal, so it falls within the 9.5 financing-equity regime: prohibited unless the 9.4 approval procedure is followed and disposal is barred during any prohibited period.
rules.evidence: Financing equity poses risks to the compliance of Aussie Broadband Persons with this Policy, particularly where the terms of the financing arrangements may place these persons in a position of conflict with their obligations under this Policy

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling for all Aussie Broadband Persons.
rules.evidence: Aussie Broadband People are not permitted to “short sell” Aussie Broadband Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy and is not listed within the 'Trade' definition.

CFDs are not named but fall within 'Derivative' (s761D derivatives and instruments limiting economic risk), so they follow the same regime as other Derivatives: banned over unvested/restricted securities, permitted over vested unrestricted securities (with prior approval for Directors/ELG/SLG).
rules.evidence: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)

rules.detail: Entering a margin loan using Aussie Broadband Securities, or transferring them into an existing margin loan account, is prohibited unless the individual first follows the 9.4 approval procedure, the loan terms prevent forced disposal during any period the Policy would prohibit trading, and any margin call is promptly reported to the Chair and Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: all Aussie Broadband Persons are prohibited from using Aussie Broadband Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including entering into margin loan arrangements in respect of Aussie Broadband Securities or transferring Aussie Broadband Securities to an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance is expressly a 'Trade' and, where done as collateral for financing, is prohibited unless the 9.4 approval procedure is followed and the same no-forced-disposal and call-notification conditions are met.
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading includes ... the grant of any encumbrance over the Securities

rules.detail: General prohibition on using Aussie Broadband Securities as collateral in any financial transaction is subject to an exception path: prior 9.4 approval, contractual terms barring disposal during any prohibited period, and prompt notification of any call made under the arrangement.
rules.evidence: Subject to paragraph 9.5(c) of this Policy, all Aussie Broadband Persons are prohibited from using Aussie Broadband Securities as collateral in any financial transaction

rules.detail: Six-month minimum holding period: sale of shares within 6 months after purchase is banned, except sale within 6 months of vesting or exercise of options/rights under an employee share scheme.
rules.evidence: Aussie Broadband People must not deal in the same Aussie Broadband Securities within a 6 month period. This means that. the sale of Aussie Broadband shares within 6 months after their purchase is prohibited by this Policy.

financing_disclosure: All Aussie Broadband Persons; trigger: entering into any financing arrangement using ABB Securities as collateral; to: Chair and Company Secretary via the 9.4 approval procedure; deadline: before entering the arrangement.
All Aussie Broadband Persons; trigger: a call made under a financing arrangement; to: Chair and Company Secretary (or Group CEO if they are the applicant); deadline: promptly.
Directors; trigger: none (company discretion); to: market/ASX (public disclosure by the company); deadline: not specified.

exemption_authority: The Chair and Company Secretary (or Group CEO where they are the applicant) may grant clearance to deal, including to dispose of securities during a Blackout Period for hardship or exceptional circumstances; refusal is final, discretionary, need not be reasoned, and must be kept confidential by the applicant. The Board may also open a Trading Window outside the normal periods where it considers the market fully informed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivative means: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly names 'collars' as a Derivative, so a bank-provided equity collar is unambiguously regulated dealing, not merely swept in by residual wording.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Financing equity poses risks to the compliance of Aussie Broadband Persons with this Policy, particularly where the terms of the financing arrangements may place these persons in a position of conflict with their obligations under this Policy and/or with the insider trading laws (e.g. if a call is made under a margin loan which results in Securities being sold while the relevant person possesses Inside Information).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's loan and collar must be drafted so a forced sale on a margin call, or on collar settlement, cannot occur while the executive holds inside information or during a Blackout Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the relevant individual must ensure that the terms of the financing arrangements do not require, or allow for, the disposal of the relevant Securities at any time when this Policy would prohibit the person from trading the relevant Securities ... and the relevant individual must promptly inform the Chair and Company Secretary of Aussie Broadband ... of any call that is made under the financing arrangements, and of the terms of that call.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's facility documents must contractually preclude enforcement sale during Blackout Periods, and any margin call must be reported to the Chair and Company Secretary promptly, which the bank should build into notice/cure mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Aussie Broadband may publicly disclose the terms and nature of any financing arrangements to which an Aussie Broadband Director is a party, and the terms and circumstances of any call made or likely to be made under those arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty is a Director, the company may publicly disclose the collar/loan terms and any margin call, which affects confidentiality expectations for the bank and executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval to trade will be confirmed in writing and is valid for five (5) business days (inclusive of the approval date) unless otherwise stated.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For Directors, ELG and SLG, the collar (and any loan) must be priced and executed within a 5-business-day approval window, requiring tight coordination with the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: individuals who wish to trade in Aussie Broadband Securities and are members of any of the following groups must first seek approval in writing ... each Director ... the Executive Leadership Group ... the Senior Leadership Group
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only Directors and senior executives (the likely collar counterparties) face the prior-approval gate; other staff can enter vested, unrestricted Derivatives without seeking clearance, subject to the general dealing rules.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this Policy, but only through the section 9.5 financing-equity gateway, not as an unrestricted right. Using Aussie Broadband shares as collateral for a loan, and entering the collar itself (since 'Derivative' expressly includes collars), is prohibited by default but becomes permitted once the individual obtains prior written approval from the Chair and Company Secretary (or Group CEO) under the 9.4 procedure, on terms that prevent the lender from forcing a sale during any Blackout Period or while the person holds inside information, with prompt disclosure of any margin call. This is only available over vested, unrestricted shares - Derivatives over unvested shares, or vested shares still subject to disposal restrictions, are banned outright. Approval lasts only 5 business days and dealing must occur within an open Trading Window, so execution must be tightly coordinated with the bank, and if the counterparty is a Director the company may publicly disclose the arrangement's terms and any margin call.
